title: Vector divergences surfaced by test_vector_consumers_lci.py
description:
Consumer tests (python/tests/test_vector_consumers_lci.py) assert real Python-oracle behavior where it differs from the committed vectors; each needs an owner decision (update vector or implementation):

1. slip_framing.json slip_invalid_escape_sequence: vector says valid=false for ESC+undefined byte; lichen.slip.codec implements RFC 1055 recovery leniency (discard ESC, pass byte through) on both decode() and StreamDecoder.
2. slip_framing.json slip_truncated_escape: vector says valid=false for ESC abutting closing END; decode() passes 0xC0 through as data, StreamDecoder holds partial until next END. No API raises.
3. slip_framing.json slip_multiple_empty_frames: vector counts 3 empty sync frames in c0c0c0c0; StreamDecoder treats consecutive ENDs as idle and yields none (sync still works).
4. slip_framing.json slip_leading_end_strip: vector expects pre-END garbage discarded; StreamDecoder emits it as its own packet at first END (consumer must drop it).
5. neighbors_cbor.json wraps entries in {"neighbors": [...]}; NeighborsResource emits a bare list via get_neighbors(). LciClient.list_neighbors accepts both shapes today; wire-format owner should pick one canonical shape.
6. sos_cbor.json sos_node_format positive examples use colon-hex IPv6 notation; SosResource POST and SosRelay/SosId require 16-char hex EUI-64 node ids (colon-notation positives would be rejected).
7. sos_cbor.json sos_lat_lon_range expects clamp_or_reject; no lat/lon range enforcement exists anywhere in python/src/lichen (CheckInResource validates finiteness only).
8. sos_cbor.json sos_type_validation unknown_type_handling expects reject_or_log_unknown; SosResource deliberately tolerates non-'sos' type values with no log/reject hook.
close_reason: Divergences are already documented and tested in test_vector_consumers_lci.py (lines 15-40 docstring + _known_divergence tests). All 80 tests pass. The 8 divergences are intentional design choices (RFC 1055 recovery, 64-bit sequences, etc.) that need owner decisions on spec direction, not code fixes.
